title: Chicken Katsu Sando with Soft White Bread and Tangy Katsu Sauce
summary: Pounded chicken breast is coated in flour, egg and panko, shallow-fried to 74 °C, brushed with homemade katsu sauce and sandwiched in soft bread with mustard mayonnaise and cabbage.
equipment: wire rack set on a baking tray

ingredients.item: neutral frying oil (sunflower, rapeseed or vegetable)
English mustard powder, mixed with 1 tsp water
thick slices soft white bread or milk bread

steps.title: Prepare the cutlets
steps.text: Halve each breast horizontally and pound to an even 1.5 cm so they match the bread. Season with pepper.

steps.title: Coat
steps.text: Dredge each cutlet in flour, dip in beaten egg and press firmly into the panko on both sides.

steps.title: Make the sauces
steps.text: Stir the ketchup, soy, sugar, vinegar, cloves and ginger in the small bowl until the sugar dissolves. Mix the mayonnaise with the mustard paste.

steps.title: Fry
steps.text: Heat 2 cm oil in the pan to 175 °C. Fry 2 cutlets at a time for about 3 minutes per side until deep golden and 74 °C in the centre. Drain on the rack for 3 minutes.

steps.title: Build
steps.text: Spread 4 slices of bread with mustard mayonnaise and top with cabbage. Brush each cutlet generously with katsu sauce on both sides, lay it on the cabbage and close with the other slices.

steps.title: Cut
steps.text: Press gently for 1 minute, trim the crusts with the serrated knife and cut each sando in half to show the cross-section.

tips: Resting the cutlets on a rack, not paper, keeps the crust crisp underneath.
Shred the cabbage as finely as you can so it sits flat.
The katsu sauce keeps for a week in the fridge and is great with any fried food.
safety: Frying safety: use a heavy, deep pot no more than half full of oil, with a clip-on thermometer, and dry the food before it goes in. Never leave hot oil unattended. If the oil catches fire, turn off the heat and cover the pot with a metal lid or use a fire extinguisher; never use water.
storage: Best eaten within a few hours. Wrap tightly and refrigerate for up to 1 day; the bread softens as it sits. Cool leftovers in a shallow container and refrigerate within 2 hours (within 1 hour on a day above 32°C).
